stemBlocks.value: A right-angled triangle ABC has the right angle at B, with BC = x, AB = x + 7 and hypotenuse AC = x + 8, where x is positive. The acute angle θ is at C. a) Use Pythagoras' theorem to form an equation in x. b) Solve the equation and state the three side lengths. c) Determine the exact values of sin θ, cos θ and tan θ.
Think first: The longest expression, x + 8, must be the hypotenuse, so it is the one that stands alone on its side of the equation.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p172-q02 from workbook page 172.

solutionSteps.instruction: Write Pythagoras with the hypotenuse alone.
Collect all terms on one side.
Factorise and solve, rejecting the negative root.

contentBlocks.value: Opposite θ is AB = 12, adjacent is BC = 5, hypotenuse is AC = 13
Result: sin θ = 12/13, cos θ = 5/13, tan θ = 12/5

strategyBlocks.value: Square the two legs, set their sum equal to the square of the hypotenuse, solve the resulting quadratic and reject the negative root, then read off the ratios at C.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (a) x² + (x + 7)² = (x + 8)²  (b) x = 5, so the sides are 5, 12 and 13  (c) sin θ = 12/13, cos θ = 5/13, tan θ = 12/5

whyThisWorks.value: Pythagoras turns a geometric condition into an algebraic one, and because the unknown appears squared on both sides the x² terms partly cancel, leaving a quadratic that factorises cleanly. The negative root is rejected not by convention but because a side length cannot be negative. The result is the familiar 5-12-13 right triangle, whose ratios are exact fractions with no rounding at all.

commonErrors.misconception: Setting x² + (x + 8)² = (x + 7)², i.e. choosing the wrong side as the hypotenuse.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Setting x² + (x + 8)² = (x + 7)², i.e. choosing the wrong side as the hypotenuse.

commonErrors.misconception: Keeping x = −3 as a second answer instead of rejecting it.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Keeping x = −3 as a second answer instead of rejecting it.

examTip.value: In any Pythagoras equation, put the largest side by itself on one side — with algebraic sides the largest is the one with the biggest constant.

promptBlocks.value: A right-angled triangle has legs x and x + 2 and hypotenuse x + 4, with x positive. Form and solve the equation.

answerSpec.displayValue: x² + (x + 2)² = (x + 4)² gives x² − 4x − 12 = 0, so x = 6 and the sides are 6, 8, 10.
acceptedForms: x² + (x + 2)² = (x + 4)² gives x² − 4x − 12 = 0, so x = 6 and the sides are 6, 8, 10.
